strategies.name: orb_breakout_pullback_continuation
strategies.entry_summary: On the 5-minute chart with the opening range defined by the first three candles, wait for a breakout, then wait for a pullback candle that breaks into the range but closes back above it, and enter on the break of that pullback candle's high.
strategies.exit_summary: Stop loss at the bottom of the opening range (alternatively the bottom of the pullback candle); take-profit at 1.5 times risk, with tested variants sweeping 2.5 to 4.5.

entry_sequence.action: First, I switch over to the 5-minut chart. This way, I can react to price action a lot quicker.
My orb range is still defined by the first 15 minutes of the day. But since I'm on the 5-minut time frame now, I have to use the first three candles to define my range high and range low.

Once I have those defined, I then wait for my breakout just like before. But this time, I don't buy immediately on the close of this breakout candle. Instead, I have to wait and see if price is going to make a pullback towards the opening range.
what I'm looking for is a candle that's going to break through the range but then close back above it, which is exactly what this candle here has done.

Once I get this pullback candle, I don't enter immediately. I want to see confirmation that price is going to bounce off and move back up. And I'm going to be waiting for a break of this most recent high. We get that on the next candle. And this gives me my confirmation to enter into a trade. So, the trade is opened here.

confluences.description: I need to take into account the height of this breakout. And I made sure that this was greater than at least 1 times ATR to be considered a suitable breakout.
The reason for this is that I want to see buyers coming back in and pushing the price back up. That gives me confirmation that this line is now starting to act as support.

stop.description: The stop loss will still go at the bottom of my opening range.
stop.alternative: I don't have to put the stop loss down here. It could also go at the bottom of this pullback candle.

targets.description: I will target 1 and 1/2 times for my take-profit ratio.
targets.note: And likewise, I don't have to always aim for one and a half times. And I will be testing out all of these different scenarios.

targets.description: I tested take-profit ratios starting at 2 1/2 and going all the way up to 4 1/2 in increments of 0.5.

variants.timeframe_note: 5-minut chart; orb range defined by first three candles
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: wait for pullback candle that breaks through the range then closes back above it, then enter on break of this most recent high
variants.transcript_quote: I'm going to be waiting for a break of this most recent high. We get that on the next candle.

variants.target_note: take-profit ratios starting at 2 1/2 and going all the way up to 4 1/2 in increments of 0.5
variants.transcript_quote: I tested take-profit ratios starting at 2 1/2 and going all the way up to 4 1/2

variants.variant_label: stop-order at ORB top, no confirmation
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: no pullback/high-break confirmation; place a stop order at the opening range so you get in immediately when price hits it
variants.transcript_quote: should I just place a stop order at the opening range? That way, when price hits it, I get in immediately for that bounce back up.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: measure breakout from top of range but wait for price to pull back all the way into the midpoint and buy there with a stop order, no confirmation of a previous high being broken
variants.target_note: smaller stop at midpoint so less movement needed for 1.5x, or aim for even more
variants.transcript_quote: I'm waiting for price to pull back all the way into this midpoint here, and that's where I'm going to buy with a stop order.
It could also go at the bottom of this pullback candle.

instrument_classification.note: I have back tested 5 years of S&P 500 data to find out for myself.

coverage_notes: break-of-high confirmation variant — PRESENT: entry_sequence step 5 + variant 'break-of-high confirmation entry (base)'; verbatim 'I'm going to be waiting for a break of this most recent high. We get that on the next candle.'
target-R sweep 2.5-4.5 variant — PRESENT: targets[1] + variant 'target-R sweep 2.5 to 4.5'; verbatim 'take-profit ratios starting at 2 1/2 and going all the way up to 4 1/2 in increments of 0.5.'
stop-order at ORB top (no confirmation) variant — PRESENT: variant 'stop-order at ORB top, no confirmation'; verbatim 'now I'm using a stop order at the top of the orb.'
midpoint stop-order entry variant — PRESENT: variant 'midpoint stop-order entry'; verbatim 'I just enter immediately as it reaches the midpoint.'
alt stop at pullback-candle low — PRESENT: stop.alternative + variant 'alt stop at pullback-candle low'; verbatim 'It could also go at the bottom of this pullback candle.'

closing 'do the opposite / breakout momentum' idea — ABSENT-WITH-REASON: this is a future-backtest proposal, not a taught runnable setup. Speaker frames it as a next-video idea with no rules given: 'this back test gave me another idea, which is actually to do the opposite of waiting for a pullback and instead focus on the momentum and the strength of the initial breakout... I can do a back test on that idea. If you want me to make a video on it...'. No entry/stop/target taught, so it is not extracted as a strategy or variant.

SCOPE NOTE — the separate immediate-breakout strategy (15-minute ORB, buy on breakout candle close, stop at range bottom, 1.5:1) is NOT extracted here per scope; it is a distinct strategy (different entry: no pullback/continuation). The 12:00 no-entry cutoff and the too-small/too-big ATR range filter were taught only in the recap of that original 15m strategy and are not part of this pullback-continuation object's inventory, so they are excluded.
